svg.title: Separate Estimates vs Hierarchical Partial Pooling
svg.desc: Estimating each group separately lets small groups chase noise; a hierarchical model borrows strength across groups and shrinks small groups harder toward the overall mean.
svg.text: Each group on its own vs borrowing strength and shrinking toward the grand mean
None — each group is an island
The smaller the sample, the more
it shrinks to the grand mean
τ→0 full pooling, τ→∞ no pooling
Dot size = sample size — small groups are most extreme
The smaller the group, the further it moves
The smaller the sample, the more unusable the interval
No pooling believes each group's noise as well as its signal.
A hierarchical model borrows across groups and pulls small groups in hardest.
Large n: w→1, its own mean
Small n: w→0, the grand mean
Hierarchical posteriors rarely have a closed form — which is why MCMC comes next.
